docs.task: How a failed phase removes its dependents from the queue (Rule D9) in the fold and the planner, and its conformance fixture.

asks: How a failed phase removes its dependents from the queue (Rule D9) in the fold
How the same rule works in the planner

data_flow.step: The plan is approved. `adopt_plan_phases` builds one `PhaseRun` per plan phase with a fresh `WorkLoop` (`next = Idle`). `depends_on` is `Some(list)` when every listed id exists and is not the phase itself, else `None` (Rule M5: depends on every earlier phase). A phase naming a project not in the workspace starts as `Blocked` with a reason.

A phase's impl loop reaches `LoopNext::Blocked` in the fold by one of several routes: the user abandons a failed execution (`exec_gate_answered` with `retry == false`, reason `<agent> failed and the user abandoned it.`), the stuck gate answered `block` or an unrouted `fact` (`Stuck: <need>`), the review cap gate answered other than another pass, the Resolve-review judge returns `Block`, a discarded RouteAnswer falls back to Blocked, a requirement change (Rule D10) sets Blocked with `announced_block` and `block_gate_answered` already true, or the `PhaseBlocked` event itself.

Next planner pass: `Planner::phases` calls `removed_phases(s)`. Blocked impl loops seed `failed`. Each idle phase whose dependency list (or, for `None`, every lower id) contains a failed or already removed id is added to `removed`, repeated to a fixpoint, so removal is transitive. Phases that are not idle (already running or terminal) are never added.

`Planner::phases` skips every removed phase, so no spawn step is produced for it. Independent idle phases still start through the M2 and `deps_passed` checks. For the blocked phase, `loop_steps` hits the `Blocked` arm.
First pass on the blocked loop emits `Step::AnnounceBlocked`. The runner appends `SessionEvent::PhaseBlocked`; the fold sets `announced_block = true`.

Next pass, outside YOLO with `block_gate_answered == false` and `blocked_gate.is_none()`, the planner emits `Step::OpenGate` with `GatePayload::PhaseBlocked`. The fold's gate-opened arm sets `PhaseRun.blocked_gate`.

The user answers. `answer_needs_route` is true only for `retry` with non-blank text. The fold's gate-answered arm clears `blocked_gate`, sets `block_gate_answered = true`, and for `retry` resets `announced_block`/`block_gate_answered` to false, sets `extra_cap`, `resolve_rounds = 0`, and replaces `next` with `Work { kind: Fix, .. }` (or `AwaitRoute` when text was given). Because `next` leaves `Blocked`, `removed_phases` no longer seeds that phase, and its dependents return to the queue on the following pass. Any other choice (`leave`) keeps it blocked and its dependents removed. The gate-answered arm picks the test loop only if the test loop is blocked and the impl loop is not.

Readers of the removed set: `implementation_review` and `project_code_done` count removed phases as finished so the session proceeds; `view::phases` reports `PhaseStatus::Removed` and the board card `StageStatus::Skipped`; `judge_input` describes the phase as removed because a dependency failed.

patterns.description: Rule D9 adds no event and no field to `SessionState`. The fold sets a phase's `impl_loop.next` to `LoopNext::Blocked`. `removed_phases` computes, on every call, the transitive closure of idle phases whose dependencies are blocked or already removed. Because nothing is stored, a retry that moves a loop out of `Blocked` un-removes the dependents on the next pass with no extra event. Fold purity (CLAUDE.md pattern 1) and planner purity (pattern 2) both hold.
patterns.name: Derived, not stored: the removed set is a pure function of the fold

patterns.description: `Planner::phases` computes the set once and `continue`s over a removed phase, so no spawn step is produced for it. A phase that is not removed and idle starts only if its project has no busy loop (Rule M2) and `deps_passed`. Completion gates treat a removed phase as finished: `implementation_review` and `project_code_done` accept `removed.contains(id) || impl_loop.is_terminal()`, so a session with removed phases still reaches the review gate, closing stages, and completion.
patterns.name: Planner skips removed phases and consults the set in completion checks

patterns.description: When a loop's `next` is `Blocked`, `loop_steps` first emits `Step::AnnounceBlocked` (key `blocked:{phase}:{tests}`) until the fold sets `announced_block`. The runner turns the step into `SessionEvent::PhaseBlocked`, whose fold arm sets `announced_block = true` and, if the loop was not already blocked, sets `next = Blocked`. After the announcement, outside YOLO and with no earlier answer (`block_gate_answered` false) and no open gate (`blocked_gate` none), the planner opens `GatePayload::PhaseBlocked`. Under YOLO the gate is never opened (the `!s.yolo` condition), and `judge_input` records `leave` as the fixed YOLO answer for a gate that was open when YOLO switched on.

document.problem: Rule D9 (HANDOVER.md line 496) says a failed phase removes every phase that depends on it from the queue and independent phases continue. Ostra implements this as derived state: the fold records only that a phase's loop is `Blocked`, and the planner computes the removed set from the phase graph on every pass with `removed_phases`. The task is to document exactly where that happens, how a phase reaches and leaves the blocked state, and what the single conformance fixture does and does not assert.

submit.findings_summary: Rule D9 is derived state. The fold only sets a phase's impl loop to `LoopNext::Blocked`, by abandoning a failed execution, a stuck gate, the review cap, the Resolve judge, or the `PhaseBlocked` event. The pure `removed_phases` in plan.rs recomputes the transitive closure of idle dependents on every pass, and `Planner::phases`, the completion checks, the view, and judge_input all read it. A `retry` answer on the phase_blocked gate moves the loop out of Blocked, so dependents return to the queue on the next pass. The only fixture, `d9_blocked_phase_removes_dependents` (tests/conformance/main.rs:1005), covers one direct dependent and one independent phase. It does not cover transitive removal, M5 default dependencies, the phase_blocked gate, YOLO, retry un-removing dependents, or a blocked test loop, which does not seed removal.

docs.task: How gates are opened, answered, and handled under YOLO.

asks: How gates are handled under YOLO

data_flow.step: A Planner method decides a gate is due and calls `self.gate(title, explanation, payload)`, which pushes `Step::OpenGate`. `Planner::push` first applies the Rule O4 hold and, for spawns only, the budget guard, which opens `BudgetReached` once `spent_usd >= budget + budget_raised`.

The runner's driver performs the step: `perform` appends `SessionEvent::GateOpened { id: GateId::new(), title, explanation, payload }`. For `ImplementationReview` it first writes the session context file (Rule F2).

`Inner::append` stores the event, folds it, broadcasts it, and wakes the driver. `materialize` upserts the gate into the gates table, and `push_for` sends a Web Push notice unless the session is YOLO (the one exception is HarnessFailure).

The fold inserts a `GateRecord` (answer None) and calls `on_gate_opened`, which stores the gate id on the owning track, loop, phase, project track, or session field (for a PhaseBlocked gate: `phases[phase].blocked_gate`).

User path: the browser POSTs `AnswerGate { answer }`; the handler calls `Engine::answer_gate`, which validates, appends `GateAnswered { source: User, routed }`, and wakes a Permission waiter if there is one.

YOLO path: on the next planning pass `Planner::flows` sees `s.yolo` and an open gate and emits `Step::YoloAnswer { gate }` (key `yolo:{gate}`). `perform_yolo` calls `yolo_plan`; a Fixed plan appends `GateAnswered { source: Yolo, reason }` directly, a Judge plan calls the YoloAnswer judge first and validates with `yolo_answer_from_judge`. Failures append a `Note` and leave the gate open.

The fold handles `GateAnswered`: the first answer wins (a gate with an answer is skipped), the record gets answer, source, reason and answered_at, then `on_gate_answered(id, payload, answer, routed)` updates loop, spec, plan, closing, init, or budget state. A routed answer parks in `held_answers` or `LoopNext::AwaitRoute` until the Route answer judge decides.
The next `next_steps` call reads the new state and the planner emits the follow-up (a spawn, a judge, the next gate, or completion).

patterns.description: The planner never writes events. A Planner method calls self.gate(title, explanation, payload), which pushes Step::OpenGate. Step::key() for a gate is `gate:{kind_str}:{gate_owner(payload)}`, so one planning pass never emits the same gate twice and the runner does not start a step already in flight. The planner also guards re-opening with fold state (`t.approval_asked_version != t.version || t.approval_gate.is_none()`, `p.blocked_gate.is_none()`, `track.closing_gate.is_none()`). The runner performs OpenGate by appending GateOpened with a fresh GateId; the fold stores a GateRecord and on_gate_opened records the gate id on its owner (spec.approval_gate, plan.questions_gate, loop.gate, phase.blocked_gate, budget_gate, feedback.gate, project closing_gate, init approval_gate).

patterns.description: In Planner::flows, when `s.yolo` is true, every open gate that is not a Permission gate and not `yolo_leaves_open` gets a Step::YoloAnswer. Rule P1 returns before this block when the session is paused, so a paused session gets no YOLO answers. perform_yolo calls judge_input::yolo_plan: Fixed answers are appended directly; Judge plans (open_questions, spec_approval, plan_approval) call the YoloAnswer judge with a per-gate output schema and pass its answer through yolo_answer_from_judge (all questions answered, approval only with a fact-check PASS, rejection needs feedback); a judge call error or a refused answer appends a Note ('The gate waits for you.') and leaves the gate open, and the planner will emit YoloAnswer again on the next pass. The final GateAnswered has source Yolo, a reason, and routed computed by answer_needs_route. YOLO answers come out as: stuck=fix, implementation_review=done, closing_gate=defaults (tests/docs only if the request asked), fact_check_recurring=another-round while passes < 6 then stop, review_cap=another-pass, phase_blocked=leave, execution_failed=retry while fewer than 2 earlier answered ExecutionFailed gates exist for the same agent anywhere in the session (counted by agent, not by execution or phase), then abandon, harness_failure=native, skill_approval=proposal defaults, permission=AllowOnce, budget_reached=None (left open).

patterns.name: Fixed YOLO answer with a stated reason

patterns.description: POST handler -> Engine::answer_gate: loads the gate from the db, rejects an already answered gate, runs validate_answer (shape match, all questions answered, rejection needs feedback, ImplementationReview option check), checks that an approval has a fact-check PASS on the current version, adds an allow rule for 'always in this workspace', appends GateAnswered with source User and routed = answer_needs_route(payload, answer), and for a Permission gate sends the answer on the oneshot channel the waiting execution holds. validate_answer does not check the `option` string of any Choice gate except ImplementationReview; the fold treats an unknown option as the default branch (for PhaseBlocked, anything other than `retry` leaves the phase blocked). Other answer sources: set_yolo(enabled) answers open Permission gates at once with AllowOnce; recover() denies open Permission gates as source Engine at server start; the interrupt path denies the Permission gates of ended executions as source Engine; resume_execution answers an ExecutionFailed or HarnessFailure gate with `retry` after stashing a resume hint.
patterns.name: User answer path

patterns.description: on_gate_answered for PhaseBlocked clears phase.blocked_gate, sets block_gate_answered, and on `retry` restores the review budget (extra_cap = iterations), clears announced_block and block_gate_answered, resets resolve_rounds and open_before_resolve, and sets loop.next to Work{Fix} with the last review's BLOCKER, HIGH and MEDIUM findings, or to AwaitRoute (Route answer judge, then Work{Fix}) when the answer has text. Which loop is retried is chosen by `tests`: the test loop when it is blocked and the implementation loop is not. A `leave` or any other option keeps the loop Blocked with block_gate_answered = true, so the gate is not reopened.
patterns.name: Fold of an answer into loop state (phase_blocked retry)

patterns.description: answer_needs_route is the single place that decides whether an answer waits for the Route answer judge. Bare choices (approve, stop, retry or leave without text, done, raise) are applied at once. Text on a spec or plan approval, fact-check recurring (not stop), review_cap another-pass, stuck fact, phase_blocked retry, and implementation_review feedback is routed. The flag is stored on GateAnswered so the fold stays pure. A Stuck `fix` is never routed (Rule O8).
patterns.name: Rule J1 routing flag on the event

patterns.description: CLAUDE.md recipe: add the variant to GatePayload with stage() and kind_str() arms; record it in the fold (on_gate_opened, on_gate_answered); open it from the planner; decide its YOLO handling in judge_input::yolo_plan; accept its answer shape in runner::validate_answer; add a conformance fixture; regenerate TypeScript with cargo test -p ostra-core. Every match on GatePayload is exhaustive, so the compiler also forces arms in gate_owner (plan.rs), on_gate_opened and on_gate_answered (state.rs), yolo_plan (judge_input.rs), and the validate_answer matches! list, and stage() and kind_str() in event.rs. Also required by project rules: a rule citation comment, and an update of docs/internals/gates-and-judges.md (its 'Every gate kind' and YOLO tables).
patterns.name: Adding a gate kind (project recipe)

document.problem: Ostra holds every pipeline decision behind a typed gate. A gate is opened by a pure planner step, recorded as an event, folded into session state, and answered by a user, by YOLO, or by the engine. Under YOLO some gates are answered by a fixed answer, some by a judge, some are never opened, and some are left to the user. A reader changing gate behavior (for example adding or changing a retry gate for a phase) needs the exact places that must change and the exact YOLO semantics, including cases where the code and the docs page differ.
document.scope: Task: How gates are opened, answered, and handled under YOLO. This document covers the engine path of a gate (planner step, event, fold, answer validation, YOLO plan) and the per-kind behavior, with extra detail on the phase_blocked, execution_failed, stuck and review_cap gates because they govern phase retry. It does not cover the web UI cards, the push notification payloads beyond the YOLO suppression rule, or the judge prompts.
document.title: How gates are opened, answered, and handled under YOLO

submit.findings_summary: A gate is opened by a pure planner step (Planner::gate -> Step::OpenGate), recorded by the runner as GateOpened, and folded into a GateRecord plus an owner field by on_gate_opened. A user answer goes through Engine::answer_gate (validate_answer, fact-check PASS check, GateAnswered with source User and the Rule J1 routed flag). Under YOLO, Planner::flows emits Step::YoloAnswer for every open gate except Permission, BudgetReached, and a stopped-by-user ExecutionFailed, and judge_input::yolo_plan returns a fixed answer, a judge schema, or None. Several gates are never opened under YOLO. A phase_blocked gate is not opened because the planner requires !s.yolo, so YOLO only announces the block and its `leave` arm applies only to a gate already open when YOLO was toggled on. review_cap is replaced by the Resolve-review judge, and permission asks are answered inline. The docs page docs/internals/gates-and-judges.md already covers these gates, but its YOLO table implies that phase_blocked is answered `leave`. The document lists each gate's open site with line numbers, the fold behavior for phase_blocked `retry`, and the files and fixtures to update.
